question: A binary erasure channel outputs the correct input bit with probability 0.75 and an explicit erasure symbol with probability 0.25. Find its capacity in bits/use.

solution.asked: Find information retained per use at optimal input.
steps: With a uniform input, a successful delivery reveals one full bit.
An erasure reveals none about that bit and occurs with probability 0.25.
The retained average and capacity are (1−0.25)×1=0.75 bits/use.
solution.explanation: The retained average and capacity are (1−0.25)×1=0.75 bits/use.
commonMistakes: An erasure is distinguishable from a flipped bit, so its capacity law differs from a binary symmetric channel.

hints: Identify the conditions under which erasure-channel capacity applies.
Start from $ C=(1-\epsilon)\log_22 $.

verification.method: Average conditional information for distinguishable erasure outcomes, optimized by uniform input. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: Two independent fair input bits X1,X2 are mapped deterministically to Y=X1 XOR X2. Find I((X1,X2);Y) in bits.

solution.asked: Find mutual information through a many-to-one mapping.
steps: Parity is equally likely 0 or 1, so H(Y)=1 bit.
It is fixed once both input bits are known, so H(Y|X1,X2)=0.
Mutual information is 1 bit even though the pair contains 2 bits.
solution.explanation: Mutual information is 1 bit even though the pair contains 2 bits.
commonMistakes: A deterministic map need not preserve all input information when it is not one-to-one.

hints: Identify the conditions under which deterministic mapping information applies.
Start from $ I(X;Y)=H(Y)-H(Y|X) $.

verification.method: Enumerate parity-output PMF; deterministic mapping sets conditional output entropy to zero. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: A Huffman code is designed for probabilities 0.4,0.3,0.2,0.1. Find its optimal average binary length in bits/symbol.

steps: Merge 0.1+0.2=0.3, then the two 0.3 nodes to get 0.6.
Merge 0.4+0.6=1.0. The merge weights sum to 0.3+0.6+1=1.9.
This equals the mean length of depths 1,2,3,3 weighted by 0.4,0.3,0.2,0.1.
solution.explanation: This equals the mean length of depths 1,2,3,3 weighted by 0.4,0.3,0.2,0.1.
commonMistakes: Combine the smallest current nodes at each stage, including newly formed nodes.

hints: Identify the conditions under which huffman merging applies.
Start from $ \bar L_{Huffman}=\text{sum of merge weights} $.

verification.method: Independent priority-queue Huffman merge algorithm. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: X,Y are independent fair bits with joint probabilities 1/4 in every cell. Find I(X;Y) in bits.

steps: Each marginal probability is 1/2.
In every cell the ratio is (1/4)/[(1/2)(1/2)]=1.
Every log term is zero, so I(X;Y)=0 bits.
solution.explanation: Every log term is zero, so I(X;Y)=0 bits.
commonMistakes: Shared binary alphabets do not imply statistical dependence.

hints: Identify the conditions under which independence information applies.
Start from $ I(X;Y)=\sum_{x,y}p(x,y)\log_2\frac{p(x,y)}{p(x)p(y)} $.

verification.method: Direct four-cell mutual-information sum. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

question: X is a fair bit and Y is always zero, independent of X. Find H(X|Y) in bits.

solution.asked: Find remaining uncertainty after observing Y.
steps: The observation Y=0 occurs with certainty for either input value.
It therefore leaves the posterior distribution of X fair.
The conditional entropy remains 1 bit.
commonMistakes: A constant output has zero entropy but does not force the input’s conditional entropy to zero.

hints: Identify the conditions under which uninformative observation applies.
Start from $ H(X|Y=0)=H(X) $.

verification.method: Conditional PMF remains fair for the sole possible observation. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.

H(Z)=1 bit rather than four, because the components are not independent.

question: For an AWGN channel with fixed received signal power P and white-noise spectral coefficient N0, C(B)=B log₂(1+P/(N0B)). Find lim as B→∞ of C(B)/(P/N0).

steps: Let u=P/(N0B), so the normalized expression is log₂(1+u)/u.
As B→∞, u→0 and ln(1+u)/u→1.
Converting logarithm base gives limit 1/ln2≈1.442695041.
commonMistakes: Holding power fixed makes SNR decrease as bandwidth grows; it is not a fixed-SNR limit.

hints: Identify the conditions under which power-limited capacity asymptote applies.
Start from $ \lim_{u\to0}\frac{\ln(1+u)}u=1 $.

verification.method: Evaluate the normalized original capacity at very large bandwidth using stable log1p. Arithmetic checked by executable calculation/property fixtures; same-system solution review only.
